item.title: Lab Article Style Guide
item.description:
This is the reference page I can keep open whenever I write for the Lab. It collects the article structure, typography, callout boxes, attachment buttons, media blocks, and small conventions that make separate entries feel like parts of the same website.

Use this as the canonical reference

Copy the smallest pattern that solves the problem. A page should still read well as plain text; the components are there to clarify hierarchy, not decorate every paragraph.

item.title: Academic Projects at SJTU
item.description:
During my exchange period at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, I completed several coursework projects in materials science. Unlike the lecture notes shown here, these are self-contained studies developed within specific course contexts, specifically with a stronger emphasis on modelling, analysis, or literature review.

The documents below are shared as originally submitted, with only minor adjustments where necessary.

Projects

Modelling the Melting Behaviour of Pure Ni, Zr, and Ni-Zr Alloys

A molecular dynamics study (LAMMPS) of melting and phase transitions in pure Ni, Zr, and Ni-Zr intermetallics, with focus on atomistic-scale thermal behaviour.

item.title: LaTeX Notes for Politecnico di Milano
item.description:
I started using LaTeX in 2020 during my studies at Politecnico di Milano, and it has since become my main tool for academic writing. My current setup is based on Visual Studio Code with a small set of extensions and a growing collection of custom commands and snippets tailored to my workflow.

The material below is a curated selection of lecture notes and projects, highlighting examples of my typesetting and academic work rather than complete documents. Full documents are not publicly distributed; excerpts are shared for documentation purposes only.
